**Test image observations:**
- A tomato leaf with diffuse, pale yellowish-to-bleached discoloration across a large portion of the upper surface, particularly concentrated in the upper half
- No distinct circular lesions, concentric rings, or clear fungal spots
- No white powdery coating
- No obvious leaf curling or deformation
- The lower portion of the leaf retains more green coloration
- Overall texture appears mottled/washed out

**Candidate analysis:**
- **Spider_Mites**: Matches well — causes yellowish to bronze stippling/speckling that gives leaves a bleached, mottled appearance; entire areas turn pale/yellow without distinct lesion borders
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Could fit — yellowing from margins inward, but V-shaped lesions and one-sided expression are not clearly visible
- **Target_Spot**: Doesn't match — reference shows distinct small brown spots with rings; test image has none

**Comparison with Target_Spot reference:** The reference shows discrete dark brown pinpoint-to-expanding spots with concentric rings on otherwise green leaves. The test image is very different — diffuse, large-area yellowing without any such lesion structure. This rules out Target_Spot.

The diffuse pale/yellow mottled appearance across a broad leaf area without distinct fungal lesions is most consistent with **Spider_Mites** causing chlorophyll loss through feeding stippling.
